rationale: This is a near-mechanical merge of two archive signals (Working-Capital-Ex Book Value plus the RECCH term from Collected-Cash Value) in which a one-period cash-flow flow item is added to a balance-sheet stock that is typically an order of magnitude larger, so the ranking will be almost entirely the previously tested hard-book yield rather than a genuinely new interaction.

The adjustment direction is internally consistent (a fall in DP lowers the numerator, penalizing income flattered by reduced depreciation) and it converts the archive's weak multiplicative depreciation trap into a coherent continuous yield, though the signal risks being dominated by plain earnings-to-price given DP changes are usually small relative to IB.

APALCH is already a first difference, so DELTA(APALCH/at) is a second difference of a noisy cash-flow detail item, and the change is a cosmetic temporal tweak to an archive signal whose portfolio alpha (+2.08 t-stat) already contradicted the hypothesized negative sign rather than a diagnosis of that contradiction.

Subtracting the small TXACH timing item leaves the signal essentially the long-published cash-flow-to-price value anomaly, while inheriting the sparse coverage of cash-flow detail items — a large loss of sample for a negligible economic adjustment.

The construct is sales-to-price (a known value anomaly) with an arbitrarily scaled denominator penalty built from a second difference of the heterogeneous AOLOCH flow, so any result will be hard to attribute to the claimed "reporting instability" mechanism rather than to S/P itself.

DELTA of net operating working capital scaled by assets is the standard Sloan working-capital accrual, and interacting it with book-to-market largely rediscovers the documented value–accruals interaction while reusing the exact functional template of the archive's Under-Depreciation Book Trap with a different accrual proxy.
